body.html: The Quarter Ratchathewi — who it's for at a glance — the shortest way to put it: The Quarter Ratchathewi by UHG is a boutique hotel for anyone who wants to stay "right in the middle of everything" in Bangkok without paying five-star prices in the middle of Siam · It isn't a riverside resort that whisks you out of the city, and it isn't a budget hostel — it's a new 4-star boutique hotel by UHG (U Hotels Group) on Phetchaburi Road in Ratchathewi, just a few steps from BTS Ratchathewi and one stop from Siam · The building only opened recently, and plenty of 2025 reviews still call it "brand new," so it has the edge on cleanliness and rooms that look fresh · It's still open and performing very well — TripAdvisor ranks it near the top, at #138 of more than 1,382 hotels in Bangkok, and it has earned a Travelers' Choice award · Real reviews line up on who fits here: couples, solo travelers in town to sightsee and shop, small families, and first-timers to Bangkok who want a location that walks easily to BTS and the big malls — more than people chasing quiet or a large suite-sized room · Another group that says they loved it is travelers who ride the BTS everywhere every day, because staying right by a station saves both time and transport costs in a city as notorious for traffic as Bangkok

Location and getting around — this is The Quarter Ratchathewi's number-one selling point, no question · The hotel sits at 388 Phetchaburi Road in Ratchathewi, just about a 2 min walk from BTS Ratchathewi — close enough that it counts as the main draw · Once you're on the BTS, Siam is only one stop away, putting Siam Paragon, Siam Center, and Siam Discovery within a few minutes · Plenty is walkable too: MBK Center and Siam Paragon are about an 8 min walk, while Jim Thompson House is about a 6 min walk · For souvenir and clothes shopping it's handy as well, since Pratunam Market and Platinum Fashion Mall are about a 15 min walk · TripAdvisor gives the area a walkability score of 100 out of 100, which is very rare for Bangkok · For longer trips: you can ride the BTS straight to Asok, Phrom Phong, or Thonglor without a string of transfers, and connect to the MRT at several points to reach the Silom-Sathorn side or Yaowarat · For the airports: Don Muang (DMK) and Suvarnabhumi (BKK) are about a 30-50 min drive depending on traffic · One thing to know before booking is that the stretch of Phetchaburi Road in front of the hotel has on-and-off roadworks, which several reviews mention can bring some dust and traffic noise at times, and Phetchaburi Road backs up quite a bit during rush hour — so if you order a Grab in the evening leave extra time, or take the BTS instead, which is faster
"It's a two-minute walk from BTS Ratchathewi to the hotel, and the next day Siam is one stop away for a mall day — the location alone is worth it. The rooms are new and very clean too."

Room types and decor — The Quarter Ratchathewi has 99 rooms in total, which makes it a compact hotel and keeps the atmosphere from getting too crowded · Starting with the Superior Room at about 23 sqm, available with a double bed or twin beds, it's a compact but well-laid-out entry room, good for solo travelers or couples who use the room mainly to sleep after a full day out · Move up to the Deluxe Room at about 30 sqm and it's clearly roomier, with some versions coming with a shower · The largest is the Two Bedroom Suite at about 56 sqm with two bedrooms, ideal for families or groups of friends who want to stay together · The decor is warm contemporary, working in peach, deep green, and woodwork in line with the U group's design concept, and it looks clean and modern · Every room has air-conditioning, a flat-screen Smart TV, a fridge/minibar, a safe, and free drinking water · Many reviews agree that the rooms and bathrooms are very clean, the beds are comfortable, and everything looks new because the hotel just opened · Many bathrooms use terrazzo tile and have a separate glass shower zone, with good-quality toiletries · Some rooms have a balcony or open space for natural light · For anyone here to work, the in-room desk and free high-speed Wi-Fi also draw praise · One small tip: the Superior is fairly compact, so if you want more room for luggage or you're staying several nights, consider stepping up to the Deluxe — it's more comfortable

Facilities, pool, and spa — the most-talked-about highlight at The Quarter Ratchathewi is the rooftop infinity pool (around the 8th floor) with city views, which many reviews describe as nicely designed, in bright tones, with a wide look out over the Bangkok skyline · Late afternoon into the evening is the popular time for guests to head up, soak, take photos, and sit out in the breeze · There are sun loungers and a poolside lounge corner to take it easy · On the wellness side there's a gym with modern equipment for anyone who wants to work out mid-trip · And there's a spa / Royal Thai massage service to unwind after a full day of sightseeing or shopping · On top of that there's a coffee shop, laundry/dry-cleaning, free parking, 24-hour tourist assistance, and free high-speed Wi-Fi everywhere · To be straight about it, the rooftop pool is more about the atmosphere and the view photos than a long lap pool for serious swimming, and because it's a 99-room hotel the common areas aren't resort-sized — but in terms of being fresh, clean, and offering a rooftop setting in the middle of the city, it does well above its price for the 4-star level

Food and bar — the hotel has a restaurant and coffee shop serving Thai and international dishes, and it doubles as the breakfast spot for guests · What draws heavy praise in real reviews is the breakfast, which many say is tasty, fresh, and varied, with Thai, Asian, and Western options to start the day well before heading out — it's something Ratchathewi-side reviews speak about more positively than at several hotels in the same group · The breakfast corner is decked out in warm peach tones and is nice to sit in, with fresh fruit, bread, drinks, and hot dishes · For other meals, the hotel's location helps a lot, because a few minutes' walk reaches the Siam, Ratchathewi, and Pratunam areas packed with mall food courts, street-food stalls, and well-known restaurants, so many people choose to eat out and get a taste of the neighborhood · There's a coffee shop in the hotel for an easy cup of coffee or a light drink · Overall, the food here is a small strength that rounds out the stay, especially the breakfast that earns steady praise, while for other meals using the location to explore the surrounding area is the most fun option

Service — service is another point that earns steady praise in real reviews, and a big reason the overall score is high · Several front-desk staff get mentioned for being friendly and helpful — with check-in, recommending places to eat and visit, calling cars, and looking after first-timers to Bangkok · Many reviews use the words "super kind" and "always helpful," which reflects the warm service style of the U group · The 24-hour tourist assistance, luggage storage before/after check-in, and attention to small details leave a lot of guests feeling they got more than the 4-star price would suggest · But to be straight, because it's a new 99-room hotel, some voices in the reviews say the response at certain times can be a bit uneven, especially when guests are coming and going at once or the hotel is full · Overall, service is still a clear strength here

What real reviews say (praise and gripes) — pulled together from Trip.com, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: a location that's about a 2 min walk to BTS Ratchathewi and one stop to Siam, rooms and bathrooms that are very clean because the hotel is new, comfortable beds and rooms that look new and modern, tasty and varied breakfast, a good-looking, well-designed rooftop pool with city views, and friendly, very helpful staff · On the gripes side: the most-mentioned thing is the roadworks on Phetchaburi Road in front of the hotel, which bring some dust and traffic noise at times · Next is the fairly compact Superior Room at about 23 sqm, which some feel is small for a multi-night stay or with lots of luggage, plus pricing that some reviews say climbs fast in high season, and a team whose response at certain times isn't entirely consistent — as you'd expect from a newly opened hotel · Most of these gripes can be sorted out by picking the right room, picking the right floor, and setting your expectations correctly, rather than being big problems that keep people from coming back

"The room was very clean since it just opened, the staff were lovely and genuinely helpful, and breakfast was tasty with lots to choose from · The only knock is the roadworks out front with some dust, but once you're in the room it's no problem. We'll be back next time."

Price and value — the starting price for a Superior Room is about THB 1,700-1,900/night in the normal range (around US$50-54 as shown on Trip.com), and it can climb to roughly THB 2,800-4,500+ in high season or over long weekends · A larger room like the Deluxe runs from about THB 2,400 up, and the Two Bedroom Suite for families lands in the several-thousand to low-five-figure range depending on size and season · Compared with hotels in the Siam-Ratchathewi area that also walk to the BTS and the big malls — most of which are priced well above this — The Quarter Ratchathewi feels very good value among prime-location hotels you can actually afford, especially once you factor in the newness of the rooms, the cleanliness, the rooftop pool, the well-reviewed breakfast, and a location that saves both time and transport money · If you plan to use Bangkok as a base to walk around Siam, shop Pratunam, and ride the BTS all over the city every day, every baht you put toward this location pays you back in full · As for anyone who wants a large suite-sized room or the full set of facilities of a big chain hotel, you may need to compare options in a higher budget

Good to know before booking — a few things help the stay go more smoothly · One, Phetchaburi Road in front of the hotel has on-and-off roadworks, so if you're sensitive to noise or dust, ask for a higher floor or a side that doesn't face the main road right when you book · Two, the Superior is compact at about 23 sqm, so for a multi-night stay or lots of luggage, step up to the Deluxe at about 30 sqm for more comfort · Three, make the most of the location by walking to BTS Ratchathewi instead of ordering a car at rush hour, because Phetchaburi Road jams up and the train is faster · Four, in Bangkok's high season (November-February) prices move up quickly, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms · Five, choose free cancellation while your plans are still uncertain, since prices often change by season — and don't forget to head up to the rooftop pool in the evening to see the city when the lights come on

The verdict — from all the real reviews, The Quarter Ratchathewi by UHG is the best fit for anyone who wants to stay in the heart of Ratchathewi-Siam on an affordable budget, with new, clean rooms, a rooftop pool, and a location that walks easily to BTS and the big malls · The two-minute walk to BTS Ratchathewi, one stop to Siam, walking distance to MBK and Jim Thompson House, plus the newness of the building and a well-reviewed breakfast, make it good value that's hard to match at the same price · If you're after resort-style quiet outside the city, or want a flawless large suite-sized room, this may not be the answer, and you should look at a big chain hotel or a riverside resort instead · But for a city trip where you want the best possible location to explore Siam and shop, along with new rooms and the attentive service of the UHG group — The Quarter Ratchathewi answers that need almost completely, which is why it scores high and earned a Travelers' Choice award despite only opening recently

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — The Quarter Ratchathewi by UHG

faq.q: Where is The Quarter Ratchathewi by UHG · is it far to walk to the BTS?
faq.a: The hotel is at 388 Phetchaburi Road, Ratchathewi, in the heart of the Ratchathewi area · It's about a 2 min walk from BTS Ratchathewi and one stop to Siam · It's about an 8 min walk to MBK Center and Siam Paragon, about 6 min to Jim Thompson House, and about 15 min to Pratunam Market

faq.q: Does The Quarter Ratchathewi have a pool · what floor is it on?
faq.a: Yes — there's a rooftop infinity pool (around the 8th floor) with bright, good-looking design and views over Bangkok — a popular spot to chill and take photos in the evening that many reviews praise · There's also a gym and a Thai-massage spa

faq.q: What's the starting price at The Quarter Ratchathewi · what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,700/night for a Superior Room of about 23 sqm in the normal range · There's a Deluxe at about 30 sqm (some versions with a separate shower) and a Two Bedroom Suite at about 56 sqm for families · High-season prices (Nov-Feb) climb fast, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who is The Quarter Ratchathewi for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for couples, solo travelers, and small families who want to stay in the heart of Ratchathewi-Siam on an affordable budget, walk easily to BTS and the big malls, and like new, clean rooms and a rooftop pool · If you're after resort-style quiet or a large suite-sized room, a riverside resort or a big chain hotel may suit you better

faq.q: What's the noise and the roadworks out front like?
faq.a: Several reviews mention that Phetchaburi Road in front of the hotel has on-and-off roadworks, which bring some dust and traffic noise at times · If you're sensitive to noise, it's best to ask for a higher floor or a side that doesn't face the main road right when you book · Most say it's no problem once you're in the room

faq.q: What's the breakfast like at The Quarter Ratchathewi?
faq.a: Breakfast is included in the room rate and served at the Thai-international restaurant · From real reviews, the breakfast earns praise for being tasty, fresh, and varied, with Thai, Asian, and Western options · It's something reviews speak about positively and consistently, and if you want a taste of the area, a few minutes' walk reaches Siam and Pratunam with plenty of good places to eat
